summary: This article surveys a new wave of emerging performance artists, mostly with works dated from September to December 2023, who move beyond traditional theaters into warehouses, rooftops, streets and digital spaces. It groups them by theme: new physical spaces, dance as rebellion, sound, audience interactivity, technology, and socially purposeful storytelling. The piece argues that these artists dissolve the line between stage and audience and are redefining what performance art is.
one_line: Profile of emerging performance artists in late 2023 who use unconventional spaces, interactivity, technology and social themes to challenge traditional performance.
key_facts: Alec Ramirez, 24, transformed an abandoned warehouse into an immersive 'theater' on October 15th with his piece "Converse in Verse", which invited passersby to be spectators and contributors.
Maria Zhang's project "Rooftop Rhythms", initiated on November 29th, stages interpretive dance and spoken word on city rooftops against the skyline.

James "Lightfoot" Harris and his crew blend breakdance, krumping and martial arts; their performance "Battlefield Within" on December 3rd portrayed internal struggles and the fight for personal freedoms.
Chloe Park's "Pavement Patterns" debuted on September 21st and consists of unannounced flash-mob-style street performances by a troupe of dancers, expressing connectivity and urban isolation.
DJ Vex gave impromptu gigs, most notably on October 5th at the City Park, remixing everyday sounds with electronic beats.
Emma Liu's "Silent Crescendo", premiered on November 12th, juxtaposed silence with sporadic bursts of sound to contrast digital society's noise with the human need for quietude.
Leo Torres introduced "Dialogues in Motion" on September 10th, in which viewers move alongside performers in a choreographed yet spontaneous dialogue.
Katie Simmons' "Sensory Threads", launched on December 16th, let the audience affect the performance outcome through touch, sound and scent.
Julian Fletcher's "Virtually Yours", unrolled on September 30th, is a VR experience in which the story changes with participants' decisions.
Zara Patel's "Insta-Moments", running since September 17th, uses Instagram to create a live documentary of her street performances, including the audience's reactions.
Benjamin Brooks' "Urban Echoes", showcased on November 22nd, explored homelessness by turning statistics into human stories.
Luna Martinez's "Chroma Chronicles" on December 13th told stories of multicultural identities through costumes, music and movement.
